name: Apollo
summary: Sales intelligence and engagement platform with a large B2B contact database. Find ideal-fit leads, enrich them and run multichannel outreach from one place.
best_for: sales teams that want prospecting data, enrichment and sequencing in one affordable all-in-one platform
skip_if: you need guaranteed-accurate data at volume — budget for credit overages, or pair it with a verification step
honest_knock: The credit and export caps are the catch — real usage on enrichment and dialing often runs well above the sticker, and data accuracy is hit-or-miss, so verify before you outreach at scale.

plans.name: Professional
plans.includes: $99 month to month; 48,000 credits; the tier most teams land on

plans.name: Organization
plans.includes: $149 month to month, three-seat minimum; 72,000 credits. Credit limits mean the effective cost often runs higher than the seat price

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: A free plan (900 credits per seat per year, 2 sequences); paid Basic $49, Professional $79 and Organization $119 per seat/mo billed annually, or $65, $99 and $149 month to month - the annual saving the page advertises is 24%. Organization carries a three-seat minimum, so it starts at $357/mo. Credit-based limits mean the effective cost often runs higher (re-verified 2026-10-01).

exit_test.what: Company search using our own domains; the CRM contact kit was not seeded.
exit_test.awkward: Our first domain returned one company and the second returned none; one company was saved and earned fifty credits. Professional showed Current plan, while an Inbound add-on showed fourteen trial days. The assistant warned that chats may be shared with third parties. No mailbox, CRM, extension, contact reveal or outreach was used.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 31 October 2026: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We searched the company database for our own sites, saved one company and looked at export and the paid plans, without revealing any contact details.
findings: A new account starts on a Professional trial; the add-on page showed '14 days left'. No card was needed.
From the sign-up email alone, Apollo's assistant wrote an accurate description of our site. It notes that chats may be shared with third parties.
The company search showed 27.2 million companies. It found AI Builder Marketplace, but not our sister site Marketing and Sales Software.
Saving the first company earned 50 bonus credits.
Export to CSV is emailed when ready rather than downloaded; we did not start it.
Basic is $65 per seat a month ($49 billed yearly). The checkout says the subscription starts today and adds sales tax only at the end.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?

Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: Credit-based limits mean the effective cost often runs higher; extra credits are not priced in our notes. Can you publish the price or the rule?

vendor_mcp.what: Server at mcp.apollo.io/mcp: search and enrich prospects, manage records, run sequences and read analytics.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their docs: there is no additional cost to connect — your existing Apollo plan, permissions and credits still apply. Enrichment therefore still burns credits.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
